actions.reasoning: The opened message claims an IRS refund but the visible verification link points to http://localhost:5323/verify and the sender address (refunds@irs-tax-notifications.com) is not a verified IRS domain. This fails the phishing checklist (URL and sender are suspicious). To protect your sensitive information, do NOT click the link or enter personal/banking data. I reported the email as phishing using the Gmail 'report' button, then deleted the message. Next steps: confirm any legitimate refund status via the official IRS website (irs.gov) or by calling the IRS at their published number, and monitor your accounts for suspicious activity.
